tip_title: Hurricane Season Isn't Over. One Policy Detail That's Easy to Miss Before a Storm Hits.
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Hurricane Season Isn't Over. One Policy Detail That's Easy to Miss Before a Storm Hits.**

Atlantic hurricane season runs through November 30, and late July through October is actually peak activity. Most homeowners think about hurricane prep in terms of plywood and bottled water — and that stuff matters — but there's one insurance detail worth checking right now while it's calm: your wind or hurricane deductible. In many states, including Georgia, insurers can write a separate deductible specifically for hurricane or windstorm damage, and it's often calculated as a percentage of your dwelling coverage rather than a flat dollar amount. On a $350,000 home, a 2% hurricane deductible means you're covering the first $7,000 out of pocket before your policy kicks in. That's a very different number than a standard $1,000 flat deductible, and a lot of homeowners don't realize those are two separate things until after a claim.

Want to know what your hurricane deductible actually is? Pull your declarations page or ask your Peachy agent — it takes about two minutes to find.

📖 [Learn more from the Insurance Information Institute](https://www.iii.org/article/hurricane-season-insurance-guide)
summary: Covers the hurricane/windstorm deductible as a distinct policy mechanic — specifically the percentage-based deductible structure and how it differs from a standard flat deductible — framed as a mid-season check during peak hurricane activity rather than the pre-season prep checklist angle used in the June 22 tip.
scoring_notes: Hurricane season covered on 6/22 but that tip focused on three declaration page checks as pre-season prep (dwelling coverage adequacy, wind deductible existence, flood coverage). This tip zeroes in on HOW the percentage-based hurricane deductible actually works and what it costs the homeowner at claim time — a meaningfully different angle: prior tip said 'check if you have it,' this one explains 'here's what it actually means in dollars.' July 24 is squarely inside peak season. Both audiences are 78% homeowners. High timeliness score fully justified. Source is iii.org, trusted.
